title: Wrote My Very First Line of Code
description: I typed print('Hello, World!') in a Python shell after weeks of curiosity. Seeing the machine execute something I typed felt like magic. That evening turned into an all-nighter learning about variables, conditional statements, and loops.
achievement: Completed basic Python syntax and solved first 20 practice logic problems
learned: Programming isn't about memorizing syntax; it's about breaking down problems into logical sequences.

title: Built My First Interactive Program
description: Built an interactive terminal-based expense tracker and budget simulation. It persisted records to CSV files, handled invalid inputs with try/except blocks, and generated monthly summaries.
achievement: First program with 400+ lines of clean, structured code and error handling
learned: Edge cases will break everything if you don't anticipate user behavior and data format changes.

title: Discovered the Web: HTML & CSS
description: Realized that my command-line tools needed a face. Dove into semantic HTML, CSS layout systems (Flexbox and Grid), responsive design patterns, and typography. Recreated classic web interfaces from scratch.
achievement: Built 5 responsive multi-page web layouts without frameworks
learned: CSS is easy to start, but mastering layout flow, specificity, and responsiveness takes serious architectural discipline.

title: Embraced JavaScript & DOM Manipulation
description: Moved into asynchronous programming, Event Listeners, Fetch API, and dynamic DOM manipulation. Built interactive dashboards, mini-games, and dynamic calculators with zero dependencies.
achievement: Built a client-side Pomodoro & Task tracker with real-time audio and persistent state
learned: Understanding the JavaScript Event Loop, closures, and promises is crucial before touching any external library.

title: Started Competitive Programming & Algorithms
description: Committed to solving algorithmic problems daily on LeetCode and Codeforces. Studied time and space complexity, binary search, two-pointer techniques, recursion, and graph traversals.
achievement: Solved 200+ problems, earned 50-day consistency badge, and reached Top 25% in weekly contest
learned: Brute force works, but finding an optimal O(n log n) or O(n) solution teaches true computational elegance.

title: First 48-Hour Hackathon
tagline: High pressure, sleepless night, high reward
description: Teamed up with two developers to build 'StudySync', a real-time collaborative workspace for students. Responsible for the backend API routes, JSON parsing, and client-side view binding.
achievement: Awarded 'Best Community Impact' runner-up among 42 participating teams
learned: Communication and rapid Git branching hygiene under extreme deadlines are just as vital as clean code.

title: Mastering Backend Architecture & Flask
description: Deepened backend engineering skills: routing, blueprints, authentication workflows, database schemas, template rendering engines, middleware, and secure API design.
achievement: Engineered a full-featured Markdown Knowledge Base with full-text search and tag relations
learned: Separation of concerns between business logic, data models, and view presentation keeps projects maintainable.

title: Architecting Larger-Scale Systems
description: Currently focusing on data visualization, asynchronous task queues, modular application patterns, performance profiling, and building tools that other developers can rely on.
achievement: Maintained 350+ problem solutions catalog and shipped this comprehensive coding documentary
learned: Code is read ten times more often than it is written. Craftsmanship is in the details, simplicity, and architecture.

title: Open Source Contributions & Distributed Systems
description: Diving deep into distributed caching, WebSockets at scale, and making meaningful contributions to open-source developer tooling and Python web ecosystems.
achievement: Targeting first accepted pull request in a major open-source repository
learned: The learning journey never stops. Curiosity is the true engine.
